lede: Mountain Village Council meets Thursday with a resolution that sets a sale price appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — the kind of fine print that decides whether affordable housing actually stays affordable or quietly slides out of reach. The same day, Telluride's Planning and Zoning Commission gets its first formal look at the school district's employee housing proposal on the middle-high school site, and the BOCC sits as the Housing Authority to take up regional compliance procedures. School starts Tuesday, and the first-day energy is real.
